pr.title: coverage: Use a query to identify which counter/expression IDs are used
pr.description:
Given that we already have a query to identify the highest-numbered counter ID in a MIR body, we can extend that query to also build bitsets of used counter/expression IDs. That lets us avoid some messy coverage bookkeeping during the main MIR traversal for codegen.

This does mean that we fail to treat some IDs as used in certain MIR-inlining scenarios, but I think that's fine, because it means that the results will be consistent across all instantiations of a function.

---

There's some more cleanup I want to do in the function coverage collector, since it isn't really collecting anything any more, but I'll leave that for future work.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, the `coverage_ids_info` query only computed `max_counter_id` from the maximum `CounterIncrement` found in a MIR body. During LLVM codegen, `FunctionCoverageCollector` separately maintained `counters_seen` (initially empty) and `expressions_seen` (initially filled, then direct `MappingKind::Code(CovTerm::Expression(id))` mappings removed); `append_instr` marked IDs seen when `CounterIncrement` / `ExpressionUsed` statements were encountered, and after traversal unseen IDs were rewritten to zero. The query and codegen traversal were therefore two separate sources of truth.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation to avoid is using per-instance codegen traversal as the sole source of `seen` IDs: initialize `counters_seen` empty, initialize `expressions_seen` filled except for expressions directly used by `Code` mappings, mark IDs only when coverage statements are appended for that particular instance, and zero any ID not seen in that traversal. This makes coverage-map output depend on which instantiation/CGU was traversed, so IDs omitted or moved by MIR inlining can become `Zero`; the old test expectations show this as `rhs = Zero` and `Code(Zero)`/highest `c0` for `inline_dead::live::<false>`, and `Code(Zero)`/highest `c1` for `let_else_loop::loopy`. The replacement is to derive both bitsets in the `InstrumentCoverage` `coverage_ids_info` query from the function's coverage info/MIR and consume them with an explicit `!is_used` override for unused functions.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust code compiled with coverage instrumentation where MIR contains `FunctionCoverageInfo` with counters, expressions, and mappings. Relevant inputs include generic functions instantiated more than once, functions affected by MIR inlining, functions whose coverage statements are removed by MIR optimizations, and functions that are never used. The decision depends on `CounterIncrement` and `ExpressionUsed` coverage statements, ordinary `MappingKind::Code` expression mappings, branch/MC/DC mappings, and `is_used` status; it does not depend on executing the compiled program.
analysis.summary: The PR moves coverage counter/expression "seen" tracking from codegen's per-instance MIR traversal into `CoverageIdsInfo` computed by the `coverage_ids_info` query. Codegen then uses those query bitsets to zero mappings, with unused functions always zeroed. This is an optimization/cleanup with intentional behavior changes for MIR-inlining/instantiation cases; it is not presented as a confirmed bug fix.
analysis.trigger: A coverage counter or expression is present in a function's coverage info/MIR but is absent from the codegen traversal of a particular instantiation, for example because of MIR inlining or instantiation-specific optimization, or because the whole function is unused. The old per-instance sets then classify the ID as optimized away and rewrite it to `Zero`, whereas the query-based result is consistent across instantiations.
preconditions: Coverage instrumentation is enabled and the MIR body has `FunctionCoverageInfo`.
The function contains coverage counters/expressions and mappings, including ordinary code mappings that may directly use expression IDs.
MIR inlining, instantiation-specific optimization, or dead/unused functions can make a codegen traversal observe a different set of coverage statements than the function's coverage info/MIR.
Codegen must still emit a valid coverage map and `llvm.instrprof.increment` num-counters argument for the instance.
pitfalls: Do not equate 'not seen while traversing this instance' with 'optimized away in the function'; query results are intended to be consistent across all instantiations.

When initializing expression tracking, only direct `MappingKind::Code(CovTerm::Expression(id))` mappings require an `ExpressionUsed` marker; branch/MC/DC expressions may not correspond to a particular control-flow point.
Expression IDs not directly used by any mapping remain initially 'seen' so LLVM can delete unused expressions if needed.
Unused functions need an explicit `!is_used` check; otherwise query bitsets could leave real counter terms in their maps instead of forcing zero.
`num_counters_after_mir_opts()` uses the highest set bit plus one, not the number of set counters; gaps below the highest used counter are still counted, as the FIXME notes.

Coverage statements can reach a crate/CGU without coverage instrumentation because of LocalCopy instantiation or MIR inlining; discarding them undercounts, and the `coverage_cx` early return is guarded by an ICE workaround comment.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the coverage-map regression tests `tests/coverage/inline-dead.cov-map` and `tests/coverage/let_else_loop.cov-map`, compiling with coverage instrumentation and comparing decoded map output. Check function mappings, expression operands, and `Highest counter ID seen`: for `inline_dead::live::<false>` the expected changed value is `rhs = Counter(1)` rather than `Zero`, `Code(Counter(1))` rather than `Code(Zero)`, and highest `c1` rather than `c0`; for `let_else_loop::loopy` the changed mapping is `Code(Counter(2))` rather than `Code(Zero)`, with highest `c2` rather than `c1`. Add paired cases covering a generic function with multiple instantiations and an unused function, and verify both old per-instance tracking and new query-based tracking against the same decoded map expectations. No compiler execution or reproduction is claimed here.
